main.description: Get the private-tier posts the requester is authorized to read, authored by the requester or by accounts the requester follows, and the reposts of such posts by the requester or by accounts it follows that are community members (a followed account that is not a member gives no repost item), newest first. A repost item carries `reason` (app.bsky.feed.defs#reasonRepost) and sorts by the repost's time, ties broken by the repost's URI; a reposter the requester mutes, or with a block either way, gives none, and a repost of a post the requester may not read leaves no trace. The ordering field of a post's own item is its `record.createdAt` (descending, ties broken by post URI); a `createdAt` later than the time of indexing plus five minutes is clamped to that bound, and the view carries the clamped value. Requires auth by a ready community member. Posts the requester may not read are omitted without distinction, as are posts by accounts the requester mutes. Audiences this AppView resolves: `list` (the audience record's members); `followers` (followers of the audience's owner who are ready members of this AppView, by the follow records it has indexed, which reflect a new follow or an unfollow within about a minute); `everyone` (every ready member of this AppView, not the network); and `nobody`. `following`: the accounts the audience's owner follows that are ready members of this AppView, by the follow records it has indexed, once it has compared them with the owner's repository. Until then, and always for an owner that follows more than 50 000 accounts, a `following` audience is read by its owner alone, and replies under it by their authors alone. An unfollow stops reads within about a minute. A `following` post appears in a reader's timeline only when the reader also follows its owner. When neither the owner nor a replier is a ready member, and this AppView is not indexing public records, the owner's follow of the replier is not indexed, so that reply is read by its author alone. Any other mode is served to its author only. A block record or a private block between the reader and the author, or the audience's owner, in either direction, keeps the reader out; a block through a list does not. A post under another account's audience, on any PDS, is served to anyone but its author only when one of its 8 nearest ancestors, walked through stored private posts under the same audience that the reader could read, is that account's post; its author may write there (`list` or no mode: listed in `members`; `followers`: a stored follow of that account; `everyone`: always; `following`: that account's indexed follow of the author, once compared with its repository as above; any other mode: never); in every mode, neither its author nor that account blocks the other; and that account is active. A reply more than 8 levels below that account's nearest post is served to its author only.

cursor.description: Opaque, sealed pagination cursor from a previous response to the same requester. Any other cursor, including the unsealed createdAt::key form of earlier versions, is rejected with InvalidRequest; start the feed over.

Present whenever more candidates remain; a page may be short or empty and still carry one. Absent at the end of the feed, and also, exceptionally, when the last examined position is too long to seal (an author whose did:web is several hundred characters), where the feed ends early.

errors.name: NotEnrolled
errors.description: The caller is not a community member of this AppView.

errors.name: NotReady
errors.description: The caller's account indexing is still in progress.
